first.rationale: Two declines (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) point at the same funnel stage, and two inherited memories (31, 86) say friction reduction fixes it, so onboarding simplification is the highest-leverage single slot this week. But both of those memories are measured on proxy outcomes — activation rate, completion rate, time-to-value — not on qualified revenue, which is the stated objective. That gap is exactly why memory_31 is worth a verification pull: its mechanism is cutting required signup fields, and fewer fields plausibly degrades lead qualification, which would collide with memory_44's finding that enterprise pipeline quality depends on the sales-assisted path. If the archived record shows the lift came from low-intent self-serve accounts that never converted, the action changes. The second pull goes to memory_73 because promotional pricing is the loudest available response to the competitor's entry pricing and the one I am most likely to be pulled toward under pressure; its recorded evidence is 'acquisition and revenue lift' with no retention, margin, or discount-cohort durability data, so discount-attracted SMB accounts could book revenue this quarter and erode it over the next several. High consequence, thin support for the objective — that is the triage criterion. I did not spend budget on memory_57 (referral incentives are not aimed at the failing stage), memory_91 (activation messaging is a plausible complement but lower-leverage than the upstream fix), or memory_86 (near-duplicate of 31; verifying 31 gives partial read on the shared mechanism). Running as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout: the underlying evidence is proxy-metric-based and roughly 50-64 days stale, and the market has shifted since. Guardrails should track downstream lead quality and enterprise demo-request volume, not just completion rate, so a proxy win that costs qualified pipeline is visible before it scales. If verification undercuts memory_31's field-cutting mechanism, fall back to memory_86's sequencing-only variant or to activation_messaging.

final.rationale: Verification resolved the two things that mattered. memory_31 survived contact with its source: signup +15%, activation +9%, and critically qualified revenue +4% with only -1% 30-day retention. That closes the proxy-versus-objective gap I flagged — the lift is not merely a completion-rate artifact, it carries through to the actual objective, and the retention cost is small enough not to be a durability concern. memory_73 broke in exactly the way I suspected and worse: +18% qualified revenue bought with -12% 30-day retention, and the source record itself carries an explicit instruction not to generalize targeted discounting as sustainable growth because the acquired cohort does not survive first renewal. That is the loudest available response to the competitor's entry pricing and it is now ruled out on the record, not on my intuition. Answering the competitor's discount with our own would book a visible quarter and hand back the revenue at renewal, which is the opposite of the stated objective. So the slot goes to onboarding simplification, scoped to SMB. Upgrading from small_guarded_test to standard_experiment because the confirmatory evidence is now direct rather than proxy — but scoped, not broad, for two reasons the archive was explicit about. First, exp_31 states it holds on SMB and was not replicated on other segments, so the finding does not license a cross-segment rollout. Second, memory_44 says enterprise pipeline quality depends on the sales-assisted demo-request path, and my original worry was that cutting signup fields degrades lead qualification; the clean way to honor both is to exclude the enterprise path entirely and leave demo-request intact. Guardrails: track qualified revenue and 30-day retention as primary, not completion rate, since exp_73 is the standing proof that a headline acquisition number can conceal cohort rot; hold enterprise demo-request volume as a non-inferiority check. Residual uncertainty I am not pretending away: exp_31 is 64 days old and predates the competitor's entry pricing, so the -1% retention figure was measured in a market where price-sensitive SMBs had fewer exits. If retention degrades materially past that baseline, the read is contaminated by churn to the competitor rather than by the intervention, and the fallback is memory_86's sequencing-only variant or memory_91's activation messaging, which addresses the -6% activation decline without touching signup qualification at all.
